investigations.name: action-switching
investigations.title: Action Switching in Embodied Agents (Agmon & Beer 2014)
investigations.question:
Can a single CTRNN agent with internal metabolic state autonomously switch
between two foraging actions — approaching two different chemical resources to
keep two nutrient levels alive — purely through the dynamics of its coupled
brain-body-environment system, with no higher-level action-selection
mechanism?
investigations.hypothesis:
An agent evolved for longevity in a world with two depleting nutrients and two
gradient resources will shuttle between the resources, engaging whichever one
replenishes the nutrient that is currently low. The switch is not a discrete
decision but a transition in the coupled system's state driven by the internal
nutrient sensors, reproducing the action switching of Agmon & Beer (2014).

investigations.name: active-categorical-perception
investigations.title: Active Categorical Perception (Beer 2003)
investigations.question:
Can an evolved CTRNN agent, embodied with a fan of ray distance sensors and a
horizontal effector, perceptually categorize falling objects by shape —
catching circles while avoiding diamonds — purely through the dynamics of its
coupled brain–body–environment system, with no internal "shape" label?
investigations.hypothesis:
A small CTRNN evolved against a catch-circle / avoid-diamond task will produce
category-appropriate behaviour across a range of object offsets: it will move
under circles (minimizing final horizontal distance) and move away from
diamonds (maximizing it), reproducing the active categorical perception of
Beer (2003). The categorization is a property of the whole BBE system — the
agent actively moves to perceive before it commits.

investigations.name: ctrnn-parameter-space
investigations.title: CTRNN Parameter-Space Structure
investigations.question:
How is the dynamical repertoire of a small continuous-time recurrent neural
network (CTRNN) — the "brain" shared by all of Beer's brain-body-environment
agents — organized as a function of its parameters (self-weights and biases)?
Where do equilibria appear and disappear, and what is the codimension-1 and
codimension-2 structure of those bifurcations?
investigations.hypothesis:
A single self-excitatory center-crossing neuron undergoes a pitchfork
bifurcation from one equilibrium to three (bistability) as its self-weight
increases past w≈4 (on the symmetric center-crossing line). Off that line the
pitchfork unfolds into two saddle-node (fold) curves that bound a cusp-shaped
bistable wedge in the (self-weight, bias) plane and meet at a cusp — the
codimension-2 organizing structure described by Beer (2006, 2022). A two-neuron center-crossing
circuit with mixed-sign mutual coupling can lose stability of its interior
equilibrium and oscillate.

investigations.name: legged-locomotion
investigations.title: Legged Locomotion — a CTRNN Central Pattern Generator (Beer & Gallagher 1992)
investigations.question:
Can a small continuous-time recurrent neural network, coupled to a single
leg over flat ground, evolve into a central pattern generator that produces
a rhythmic walking gait — a self-sustaining stance/swing cycle that carries
the body steadily forward — rather than a one-off lunge?
investigations.hypothesis:
A CTRNN evolved to maximize forward travel, with its leg angle fed back as
proprioception, will settle into a stable limit cycle: it plants the foot and
swings the leg backward to drive the body forward (stance), lifts and swings
forward to recover (swing), and repeats. The rhythm is a dynamical attractor
of the coupled brain-body system, not a scripted sequence — the signature of
a central pattern generator.

investigations.name: relational-categorization
investigations.title: Relational Categorization — Memory in Embodied Dynamics (Williams, Beer & Gasser 2008)
investigations.question:
Can a small continuous-time recurrent neural network categorize an object by
its size RELATIVE to a previously-seen one — catching the second of two
sequentially-presented objects when it is larger, avoiding it when smaller —
given that the first object is gone by the time the second appears, so the
comparison can only be made through internal memory?
investigations.hypothesis:
An agent evolved for this relative-size task will hold a trace of the first
object's size in its CTRNN state across the inter-stimulus interval and read it
out when the second object arrives, producing a relational decision with no
dedicated memory store — memory as a property of the coupled brain-body-
environment dynamics, the point of Williams, Beer & Gasser (2008).
